{{Short description|American chemist (1927–2015)}}
[[File:25th anniversary celebration commemorating the discovery of element-101. G. Choppin, Glenn Seaborg, B.G. Harvey, and Albert Ghiorso. Photograph taken March 28, 1980. BBC8807-07139. - DPLA - af8f363d95fee61acde8a270e0bc229c.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Choppin celebrating the 25th anniversary of the discovery of mendelevium with [[Albert Ghiorso|Ghiorso]], [[Bernard G. Harvey|Harvey]], and [[Glenn T. Seaborg|Seaborg]] in 1980.]]
'''Gregory Robert Choppin''' (November 9, 1927, [[Texas]], United States<ref name="uc.edu">{{cite web|url=http://www.artsci.uc.edu/content/dam/artsci/departments/chemistry/Docs/choppin.pdf |title=The 1995 Ralph and Helen Oesper Awardee : Honoring Gregory R. Choppon |publisher=Artsci.uc.edu |accessdate=2015-10-27}}</ref> – October 21, 2015, [[Tallahassee]], [[Florida]])<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/tallahassee/obituary.aspx?n=gregory-robert-choppin&pid=176203307&fhid=5827|title=Gregory Choppin Obituary|publisher=Tallahassee Democrat|accessdate=2015-10-27}}</ref> was an American nuclear chemist and co-discoverer of the element [[mendelevium]], atomic number 101.<ref name=discovery>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.98.1518|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=e53sNAOXrdMC&pg=PA101|isbn=978-981-02-1440-1|title=New Element Mendelevium, Atomic Number 101|date=1955|last1=Ghiorso|first1=A.|last2=Harvey|first2=B.|last3=Choppin|first3=G.|last4=Thompson|first4=S.|last5=Seaborg|first5=G.|journal=Physical Review|volume=98|page=1518|issue=5|bibcode = 1955PhRv...98.1518G|doi-access=free}}</ref> Others in the discovery group were [[Albert Ghiorso]], [[Bernard G. Harvey]], [[Stanley G. Thompson]], and [[Glenn T. Seaborg]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.osti.gov/scitech/servlets/purl/6468225|title=Symposium commemorating the 25th anniversary of the discovery of mendelevium (Conference) - SciTech Connect|author=Seaborg, G.T.|journal=Osti.gov|date=January 1980 |accessdate=2015-10-27}}</ref> The element was named in honor of [[Dmitri Mendeleev]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vanderkrogt.net/elements/element.php?sym=Md |title=101. Mendelevium - Elementymology & Elements Multidict |publisher=Vanderkrogt.net |date=1996-08-26 |accessdate=2015-10-27}}</ref>

Choppin received a Bachelor of Science degree in chemistry at [[Loyola University New Orleans]] and earned his doctorate in chemistry at the [[University of Texas]] in 1953.<ref name="uc.edu"/> He then worked as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], from 1953 to 1956.

While at Berkeley he co-discovered mendelevium. Video documentation of the discovery was produced by the television station [[KQED (TV)|KQED]] and can be viewed on YouTube with a new narration by Claude Lyneis.<ref>{{cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DrssJRb301k|title=Mendelevium: The Way It Was|date=5 November 2013|work=YouTube|accessdate=2015-10-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://today.lbl.gov/2013/11/04/60-year-old-film-surfaces-depicting-discovery-of-mendelevium/|title=60-Year-Old Film Surfaces, Depicting Discovery of Mendelevium|work=Lbl.gov|accessdate=2015-10-27}}</ref>

He taught at [[Florida State University]] from 1956 until 2001. He served there as Chair of the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry and was named Robert O. Lawton Distinguished Professor, "...the highest honor the Florida State faculty bestows upon one of its own."<ref name="floridastateuniversitynews">{{cite web|url=http://news.fsu.edu/More-FSU-News/24-7-News-Archive/2012/August/Nuclear-chemist-selected-as-first-Choppin-Chair-in-Chemistry-and-Biochemistry."|title=Florida State 24/7 - The News Site of Florida State University|author=Florida State University News|work=Fsu.edu|date=28 August 2012 |accessdate=2015-10-27}}</ref>

The chemistry wing of the science building at Loyola University is named for Choppin,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/tallahassee/obituary.aspx?n=gregory-robert-choppin&pid=176203307&fhid=5827|title=Gregory Choppin Obituary - Tallahassee, FL - Tallahassee Democrat|work=Tallahassee Democrat|accessdate=2015-10-27}}</ref> and the Gregory R. Choppin Chair in Chemistry and Biochemistry is an endowed chair at Florida State University.<ref name="floridastateuniversitynews"/>

Choppin is sometimes credited with co-discovering the elements einsteinium and fermium.<ref name="floridastateuniversitynews"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://careerchem.com/NAMED/Elements-Discoverers.pdf |title=Names of Scientists Associated with Discoveries of Elements of Periodic Table |author=Dr. John Andraos |publisher=Careerchem.com |accessdate=2015-10-27}}</ref>
